# Sources {#sec-sources .unnumbered .pdf-full}

Every prayer text in this book is taken from Wikipedia and is reused under
[CC BY-SA 4.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/). The
commentary around the texts is written for this book, from the material in
those same articles.

## Editorial notes

The texts are reproduced as the articles give them, with these exceptions.

**Modern Greek.** The Greek Wikipedia prints its demotic translation in
polytonic orthography with the translator's glosses in parentheses inside the
lines. It appears here in monotonic orthography with the glosses removed, and
with three forms normalised to standard modern spelling — *ἐπιτρέψῃς* →
επιτρέψεις, *ὑποκύψωμε* → υποκύψουμε, *δύναμι* → δύναμη. The article's own
text, for reference:

> Οὐράνιε πατέρα μας, νὰ δοξάζεται τὸ ὄνομά σου, νὰ ἔρχεται ἡ βασιλεία σου (νὰ
> βασιλεύῃς σὲ μᾶς, νὰ κυβερνᾷς τὴ ζωή μας), νὰ γίνεται τὸ θέλημά σου, ὅπως
> στὸν οὐρανό, ἔτσι καὶ στὴ γῆ· τὸ ψωμί μας τὸ ἀναγκαῖο γιὰ τὴ ζωὴ δῶσε μας
> σήμερα καὶ χάρισέ μας τὰ χρέη μας (τὰ ἁμαρτήματά μας), ὅπως καὶ ἐμεῖς
> χαρίζουμε στοὺς χρεῶστες μας (σ᾽ ὅσους ἁμάρτησαν σὲ μᾶς). Καὶ νὰ μὴν
> ἐπιτρέψῃς νὰ ὑποκύψωμε σὲ πειρασμό, ἀλλὰ γλύτωσέ μας ἀπὸ τὸν Πονηρό. Διότι
> δική σου (καὶ ὄχι τοῦ Πονηροῦ) εἶναι ἡ βασιλικὴ ἐξουσία καὶ ἡ δύναμι καὶ ἡ
> ἰσχὺς στοὺς αἰῶνες. Ἀμήν.

**Modern Greek transliteration.** Written for this book. The Greek Wikipedia
article does not romanise its text, and no standard romanisation targets Modern
Greek *pronunciation* rather than spelling. The scheme used is set out in the
pronunciation key in that chapter.

**Ancient Greek transliteration.** Wikipedia's own, taken from the article
verbatim for both the NA28 and the Patriarchal 1904 texts. The two differ
slightly in how they mark accents, because the article transliterates them in
two separate sections; that inconsistency is preserved rather than smoothed
over.

**Spanish liturgical text.** Assembled from the wording the Spanish article
gives for the current liturgical form, which the article presents split across
a table of the prayer's parts rather than as one continuous block.

**Line breaks.** Where an article runs the prayer as continuous prose, it has
been broken into lines at the petitions. The words are unchanged.

## Audio

Both recordings are from Wikimedia Commons, converted to mono 22.05 kHz MP3
and peak-normalised; the audio is otherwise unedited.

| Recording | Author | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| [Pater noster.ogg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Pater_noster.ogg) — spoken | Geremia | Public domain |
| [Schola Gregoriana-Pater Noster.ogg](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Schola_Gregoriana-Pater_Noster.ogg) — chant | Schola Gregoriana | [CC BY-SA 3.0](https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/3.0) |

Commons has no recording of this prayer in Spanish, Lithuanian or either form
of Greek, so those chapters are read by the voice installed on your own
device. MIDI files of *Pater noster* and *Vater unser* do exist on Commons,
but MIDI stores notes rather than words — it can carry the chant's melody and
never the text — so it is no use for reading a prayer aloud.

Neither recording has a verified cue list, so neither follows the text line by
line yet. Measured timings can be added without touching any code; the format
is documented in the [README](https://github.com/dsandovalv/lords_prayer#adding-audio).
